title: Financial toxicity among adults in their first six months of systemic cancer therapy: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: Objective: to estimate the prevalence of moderate or severe financial toxicity by group and the agreement of a distress screening checkbox with a validated questionnaire. Design: cross-sectional survey in four day units from February to April 2027, offered in three modes and four languages, with non-response weighting. Results and conclusions will be written after the survey.
introduction: Financial toxicity is common during systemic cancer therapy and associated with delayed or skipped treatment, but screening often relies on a single item.
methods: Clinic days were sampled at random and every eligible patient approached. The primary outcome was a moderate or severe score on a validated questionnaire; the checkbox closest in time was linked for the agreement analysis.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present response by group, weighted prevalence, prevalence ratios, checkbox agreement and spending.
discussion: The discussion will size a navigation service and state whether the checkbox is adequate for screening.
limitations: Patients who stopped treatment are missed; self-report; one centre.
conclusion: To be written after the survey; it will not claim effects of navigation.
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty.
